gate_results.gate: Authority conflicts: canon, timeline, state, viewpoint knowledge
gate_results.evidence: The draft creates an internally impossible training schedule: Julian says the next session is after one recovery day; Kade prepares for Thursday; the narration later says the second session occurs four days after the first; and at its end Julian schedules Thursday again.

gate_results.gate: Assigned chapter function and durable obligations
gate_results.evidence: The private, field-locked Rehab Two sessions give Kade eleven losses and then nine; Kade learns his rare Boundary architecture does not supply ordinary fighting skill, and his reciprocal diagnosis of Julian turns the relationship into mentor-peer rivalry.

gate_results.gate: Fresh re-authoring rather than close paraphrase
gate_results.evidence: The reconstruction replaces the source chapter’s replay/class/clinic/breakfast/call sequence with arena observation, negotiated medical clearance, two Rehab Two sessions, Eli’s oral reconstruction, and a laundry-room hinge. Retained facts and tactical concepts are reorganized around a different causal spine and payoff mechanism.

Kade’s successful pressure on Julian follows eleven diagnostic losses, Eli’s reconstruction, Mara’s prompt, Kade’s explicit plan, repeated failed attempts to hold it, and his prior practice reading Pike’s load commitment. He still loses and is too slow to capitalize.
Before the second session, the chapter establishes the reciprocal fee, Kade’s need to hold a working plan, Julian’s family scrutiny, and the medical stop contract.
The mat, tile boundary, rail, mirror, and center are established before action and repeatedly used to orient entries, turns, and finishes.

gate_results.gate: Combat: balance, reach, injury, equipment, ability
gate_results.evidence: Fields are locked; Julian wins through footwork, borrowed weight, leverage, and recovery denial; Kade’s fatigue and neurologic thresholds persist; the stop protocol ends the session.
Julian removes choices and borrows Kade’s weight without obvious planting; Kade experiments with environmental reference points, then announces and holds a plan to force Julian to commit.
Kade chooses to disclose and hold his plan; this forces Julian onto his left heel, exposes Julian’s under-practiced commitment, and gives both fighters a concrete next training problem.
Kade adopts communicable planning, Julian accepts reciprocal correction, and their rivalry becomes a standing mentor-peer practice.
The ending records headache two and declining, tremor, three stop-word rehearsals, continued restriction, and Park’s retained medical record.
The visible delta from eleven losses to nine and forcing Julian’s first plant follows observation, reconstruction, diagnosis, disclosure, and repeated embodied practice.
Kade absorbs repeated falls, fatigue, hip pain, tremor, visual edging, and a headache that triggers the agreed stop.
Progress changes how Kade collaborates with Eli and Mara and prepares him to communicate a plan to future House Trial teammates.

gate_results.gate: Progression: no unestablished capability resolves victory
gate_results.evidence: Boundary power never activates and Kade does not win; ordinary observation and footwork produce a limited tactical discovery.

gate_results.gate: Progression: rivals and institutions remain active
gate_results.evidence: Julian independently seeks correction under ongoing scrutiny; Park imposes and enforces medical conditions; Meridian prepares for its roster meeting.
The first session diagnoses Kade’s failures; the second tests an explicit held-plan strategy and reciprocal weakness discovery.
Kade converts the first session’s eleven losses into an articulated plan he states before acting and carries into his coordination with Mara.
Kade can continue hiding/improvising or disclose a predictable plan; later he can push through symptoms or invoke the stop word.

Concealment protects tactical surprise and emotional self-protection, while disclosure enables coordination and forces honest reciprocal learning; stopping protects health at the cost of ending the useful exchange.
Kade obtains Elena’s and Park’s consent, Julian signs the medical card, and Kade himself bears the physical cost and calls the stop.
Kade distinguishes observation from inference, tests his theory in repeated exchanges, and describes Julian’s weakness only after seeing the left-heel plant.

Julian seeks a rival who can expose a blind spot; Eli needs a stated model; Mara supplies a bounded diagnostic prompt; Sera repairs the duffel and presses communal participation; Taren pursues information access.
The ending carries the lesson into a standing Thursday session, Julian’s corrective work, Kade’s message to Mara, and the House Trial roster obligation.
The eleven-to-nine improvement measures progress but does not erase Kade’s losses, health limit, or need for collaboration.
The chapter remains in close third through Kade’s practical attention, mistaken models, bodily limits, and inferences; concealed motives are not narrated as fact.
Action geography and dialogue remain intelligible without typographic dependence; the prose contains no evident profanity, explicit sexual material, or lingering gore.
Deterministic full-manuscript count is 7,198 words. The approved action ceiling is 7,125, so the chapter is 73 words over the permitted maximum.
The manuscript contains chapter prose only, with no drafting notes, report material, or word-count metadata.

draft_evidence.quote: Tomorrow you'll be tired and you'll need a day. The day after, six.

comparison_evidence.quote: if he was going to hand it to Julian on Thursday morning... Julian was late.

findings.consequence: The later claim that the second session is four days after the first, followed by Julian scheduling Thursday again, makes the chapter’s day sequence impossible to reconcile and jars the reader out of an otherwise carefully tracked recovery schedule.
findings.repair_target: Choose one coherent calendar and align the recovery interval, Kade’s Thursday preparation, the 'four days ago' reference, and Julian’s next-session day without changing the eleven-loss/nine-loss progression.

comparison_evidence.quote: A chapter designated for fight or embodied action may use an upper tolerance of twenty-five percent.

findings.consequence: The draft exceeds the approved 7,125-word action ceiling by 73 words; this is small but remains a deterministic acceptance miss.
findings.repair_target: Remove at least 73 words without compressing action geography, the medical stop, reciprocal diagnosis, or closing relationship turn.

concerns: The assertion that nobody has taken center from Julian 'in this building since the spring' is unusually broad and may read as more canonically durable than needed, although the text distinguishes it from upper-years beating him from above.
Long alternating two-speaker exchanges are generally trackable by voice and context, but an audio proof-listen should confirm the Arena Two and first Rehab Two conversations.
strengths: The prior fresh-re-authoring defect is convincingly repaired: the chapter now has a materially different scene architecture and causal spine rather than a reskinned replay of the source.
The Rehab Two setting unifies safety, humility, action geography, and theme; 'the mat did not know his name' cleanly lands the rare-does-not-mean-skilled obligation.

Kade’s advancement has unusually clear receipts: eleven losses, an oral reconstruction, a diagnosed abandonment pattern, an explicit experiment, nine further losses, one forced plant, and a failure to capitalize.
Julian’s self-interest keeps the mentor turn credible. He wants a weakness exposed, accepts correction, and remains decisively superior.
The threshold stop preserves Chapter 12’s safety learning as behavior rather than exposition, and Julian’s immediate compliance builds trust through action.
The ending converts an individual combat lesson into team-readable planning and creates direct pressure toward the House Trial without spending its outcome.
Taren’s slightly overprecise access knowledge preserves the surveillance clue while fitting the new chapter structure.
